fieldMarks: Yellowish-brown to greyish-brown coat with white underbody
Long ears with black tips; brown face with eye rings
Tail black on top, white beneath
behavior: Mostly solitary and nocturnal, foraging roughly 7 p.m.-7 a.m.
Rests by day in shallow depressions called forms
Active year-round; summer diet grasses, herbs, crops; winter diet twigs, buds, bark
Fast and agile, up to about 35 mph
habitat: Open fields and pastures bordered by hedgerows and woodlots, often around agricultural fields.
range: Native to Europe and western/central Asia. Introduced to North America (southern Ontario, Great Lakes, northeastern US, from 1893-1912).
